title: AT&T's Dividend Costs the Company a Fixed Amount Every Quarter Regardless of Competitive Pressure From Starlink or Cable Rivals. Here's the Coverage Ratio That Actually Determines Whether It's Safe.
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: AT&T maintains a sustainable 4.4% dividend yield despite competitive pressures from cable operators and Starlink. With a 36% trailing payout ratio and 45% cash dividend payout ratio, the company has ample coverage to support its ~$2 billion quarterly dividend. Share buybacks have actually strengthened the dividend's footing, reducing dividend outlays year-over-year despite competitive threats.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: AT&T demonstrates strong dividend safety with healthy coverage ratios (36% payout ratio, 45% cash dividend payout ratio) and improving financial position through share buybacks. Despite competitive threats from Starlink and cable operators, the company's annuity-like customer revenues and oligopoly position provide solid support for maintaining its dividend.

title: AST SpaceMobile Trades Near $74. Here's The Subscriber Math That Justifies It.
author: Leo Sun
description: AST SpaceMobile, a LEO satellite developer, trades at $74 per share with a $21.5B market cap despite a 127x price-to-sales ratio. The company justifies its valuation through partnerships with major telecom carriers covering 3B+ subscribers, a $1.3B backlog, and projected revenue growth to $1.76B by 2028. Analysts expect positive EBITDA in 2027, making the stock potentially attractive for long-term investors despite near-term volatility.

Early mover advantage in growing LEO satellite market with 14% CAGR potential through 2033.

title: 3 Space Stocks That Could Turn $10,000 Into $50,000 By 2035
author: Leo Sun
description: The space logistics market is projected to grow at 19% CAGR through 2034. Three space stocks—SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and AST SpaceMobile—are highlighted as potential multibaggers that could turn $10,000 into $50,000 over the next decade, though all are considered speculative investments with significant growth potential as the industry expands.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong early-mover advantages in reusable orbital launch and satellite internet markets. CEO claims potential for $1 trillion annual revenue by 2030 (122% CAGR). Stock could rise more than fivefold over the next decade if targets are approached. However, currently trading at expensive 41x sales valuation with ongoing losses in space and AI divisions offsetting satellite profits.

Carved out defensible niche in reusable orbital rocket market with 92 successful Electron launches. Revenue expected to nearly triple from 2025 to 2028. Analysts expect adjusted EBITDA to turn positive in 2027. Potential multibagger gains and takeover target. Trading at 51x sales with high volatility but significant growth runway.

Unique business model partnering with telecom companies (AT&T, Verizon) to expand 5G coverage via LEO satellites. Revenue expected to rise more than 25x from 2025 to 2028. Plans to expand constellation from 10 to 45-60 satellites by end of 2026. Analysts expect adjusted EBITDA positive in 2027. Despite expensive 122x sales valuation, has significant growth potential.

title: Why Big Tech's AI Data Centers Are Turning to Bloom Energy for Power
author: James Brumley
description: AI data centers are rapidly expanding and require 200 gigawatts of electricity by 2030, but utility companies cannot keep pace. Bloom Energy's hydrogen fuel cell technology is emerging as a solution, offering faster deployment, water-free operation, and quieter performance compared to traditional generators. The company secured a major expansion with Oracle (2.8 gigawatts) and is seeing strong revenue growth driven by customers like Honda, AT&T, and Walmart.

title: AST SpaceMobile vs. First Majestic Silver: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: AST SpaceMobile, a satellite broadband company, is compared against First Majestic Silver, a profitable mining company. AST SpaceMobile burns $1.1B in cash annually while pursuing growth in space-based cellular networks, whereas First Majestic generates $472M in free cash flow with a strong balance sheet. The choice reflects a growth-vs.-stability investment dilemma, with AST expected to reach profitability by 2027 and First Majestic benefiting from rising silver prices.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: High-growth potential with accelerating revenue ($70.9M in FY2025 vs $4.4M prior year), strategic partnerships with major carriers (AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone), and expected profitability by 2027. However, significant cash burn and execution risks temper the outlook.

Profitable with strong financial metrics (13% net margin, $472M free cash flow, 0.1x debt-to-equity), benefiting from silver's rally (nearly tripled since 2025). Increased dividend and 40%+ projected sales growth. Commodity price volatility remains a key risk.
